column1: 65:1|For the music leader. A psalm of David. A song.\nGod, praise waits in silence for you in Zion;\nto you the vow will be fulfilled.|Retain silence beside praise, noting difficult relation; include separate title.
65:2|You who hear prayer,\nall flesh will come to you.|Keep bodily universal scope and direct address.
65:3|Wrongdoings have overwhelmed me,\nbut you atone for our rebellions.|Preserve singular me to plural our and atonement verb.

65:4|Happy is the one you choose and bring near
to live in your courts!
Let us be filled with the goodness of your house,
your holy temple.|Retain choosing, approach, residence and communal satisfaction.

65:5|With awesome deeds of righteousness you answer us,
God who saves us,
the trust of all the earth’s farthest reaches
and the distant seas.|Keep cosmic scope and righteous answer, not private assurance only.
65:6|You establish mountains by your power,\nclothed with might.|Continue direct address while preserving girding metaphor.
65:7|You still the roar of seas, the roar of their waves,\nand the tumult of peoples.|Repeat roar and parallel natural/social turbulence.
65:8|Those who live at earth’s edges stand in awe of your signs.\nYou make the places of sunrise and sunset shout for joy.|Keep geographical horizons rejoicing rather than merely times of day.

65:9|You attend to the earth and water it, enriching it greatly.\nGod’s stream is full of water.\nYou prepare their grain, for this is how you prepare the earth.|Retain third-person God within address and doubled preparation.
65:10|You soak its furrows and settle its ridges,\nsoften it with showers and bless its growth.|Preserve sequence of cultivation and rain.
65:11|You crown the year with your goodness;\nyour tracks drip with abundance.|Keep crown and tracks, not a generic prosperous year.
65:12|The wilderness pastures drip with it;\nthe hills wrap themselves in joy.|Continue abundance and clothing imagery.
65:13|The meadows put on flocks;\nthe valleys clothe themselves in grain.\nThey shout for joy—yes, they sing!|Keep land clothed and singing, not replace with human praise.
66:1|For the music leader. A song. A psalm.\nShout to God, all the earth!|Inline title retained with universal call.
66:2|Make music to the glory of his name;\nmake his praise glorious.|Retain repeated glory and name.
66:3|Say to God, “How awesome are your deeds!\nBefore your great strength, your enemies cringe.|Feigning submission rather than willing conversion.
66:4|All the earth bows before you and makes music to you;\nthey make music to your name.” Selah.|Preserve three acts and close quoted address.
66:5|Come and see what God has done,\nhis awesome dealings with humanity.|Invitation shifts from speaking to seeing.
66:6|He turned the sea into dry ground;\nthey crossed the river on foot.\nThere let us rejoice in him!|Keep sea and river distinct and past-to-present communal participation.
66:7|He rules forever by his might;\nhis eyes watch the nations.\nLet the rebellious not exalt themselves. Selah.|Follow read rise, retaining warning.
66:8|Bless our God, you peoples;\nlet the sound of his praise be heard.|International summons and audible praise.
66:9|He has kept us among the living\nand has not let our feet slip.|Keep life and stable-foot image.
66:10|You tested us, God;\nyou refined us as silver is refined.|Retain repeated refining process.
66:11|You brought us into a net;\nyou laid a crushing load on our backs.|Net plus burden remain distinct trials from God.
66:12|You let people ride over our heads.\nWe went through fire and water,\nbut you brought us out into abundance.|Preserve violent subjection and contrasting emergence.
66:13|I will enter your house with burnt offerings\nand fulfill my vows to you—|Communal voice becomes singular without invented speaker identity.
66:14|the vows my lips uttered\nand my mouth spoke when I was in distress.|Continue vow sentence with distress occasion.
66:15|I will offer you fat animals as burnt offerings,\nwith the smoke of rams;\nI will sacrifice cattle and male goats. Selah.|All animal classes and offering smoke retained.
66:16|Come and hear, all who revere God;\nI will tell what he has done for me.|Hearing invitation answers seeing invitation.
66:17|My mouth called to him;\nhigh praise was ready on my tongue.|Under tongue idiom clarified in note.
66:18|Had I cherished wrongdoing in my heart,\nthe Lord would not have listened.|Conditional claim kept, not general theory of unanswered prayer.
66:19|But God did listen;\nhe paid attention to my prayer’s voice.|Emphatic actual hearing contrasts counterfactual.
66:20|Blessed be God, who has not turned away my prayer\nor withdrawn his faithful love from me.|Preserve prayer/love double object with natural different verbs.
67:1|For the music leader. With stringed instruments. A psalm. A song.\nMay God be gracious to us and bless us;\nmay he make his face shine upon us. Selah.|Separate title and blessing face retained.
67:2|Then your way will be known on earth,\nyour salvation among all nations.|Blessing purpose extends beyond us.
67:3|Let the peoples thank you, God;\nlet all the peoples thank you.|Exact doubled communal refrain.
67:4|Let nations rejoice and sing aloud,\nfor you judge peoples fairly\nand guide the nations on earth. Selah.|Justice and guidance ground gladness.
67:5|Let the peoples thank you, God;\nlet all the peoples thank you.|Repeat verse 3 unchanged.
67:6|The earth has yielded its harvest;\nmay God, our God, bless us.|Harvest perfect and blessing wish distinguished.
67:7|May God bless us,\nand may all the ends of the earth revere him.|Concluding blessing again universal in reach.
68:1|For the music leader. Of David. A psalm. A song.\nLet God rise! Let his enemies scatter;\nlet those who hate him flee from his presence.|Keep three energetic petitions and title.
68:2|As smoke is driven away, drive them away;\nas wax melts before fire,\nlet the wicked perish before God.|Direct command within smoke/wax similes retained.
68:3|But let the righteous be glad and exult before God;\nlet them rejoice with joy.|Retain cumulative joy without flattening repetition.

68:4|Sing to God; make music to his name.\nBuild a road for the rider through the wilderness.\nHis name is YAH; rejoice before him.|Aravot wilderness chosen with cloud alternative noted; YAH short name preserved.
68:5|A father to orphans, a judge for widows—\nGod in his holy dwelling.|Keep social roles, not generic kindness.
68:6|God settles the lonely in a home\nand brings prisoners out into prosperity;\nbut rebels live in a parched land.|Rare prosperity term acknowledged, home/release/dryness contrast.
68:7|God, when you went out before your people,\nwhen you marched through the wasteland, Selah,|Keep dependent sentence across verse break.
68:8|the earth shook, the heavens poured rain\nbefore God—the one of Sinai—\nbefore God, the God of Israel.|Preserve difficult Sinai phrase and repeated before God.
68:9|You showered abundant rain, God;\nwhen your inheritance was weary, you restored it.|Land inheritance weariness and replenishment retained.
68:10|Your flock settled there;\nin your goodness, God, you provided for the afflicted.|Hayyah flock/community ambiguity noted, poor provision preserved.
68:11|The Lord gives the word;\nthe women announcing it are a great army:|Explicit feminine heralds retained.
68:12|“Kings of armies flee—they flee!\nThe woman at home divides the spoil.|Keep doubled flight and woman distributing spoils.
68:13|Though you lie among the sheepfolds,\na dove’s wings are coated with silver,\nits pinions with shimmering gold.”|Retain obscure sheepfold/dove scene rather than resolve roles.
68:14|When Shaddai scattered kings there,\nsnow fell on Zalmon.|Uncertain snow image and divine title retained with note.
68:15|A mighty mountain is Mount Bashan,\na many-peaked mountain is Mount Bashan.|Literally mountain of God, preserve doubled Bashan.
68:16|Why look with envy, you many-peaked mountains,\nat the mountain God desired for his dwelling?\nYes, the LORD will live there forever.|Personified rival peaks and chosen dwelling.
68:17|God’s chariots are tens of thousands, thousands upon thousands;\nthe Lord is among them—Sinai in the sanctuary.|Preserve difficult Sinai clause without inserting journey.
68:18|You went up on high, leading captives away;\nyou received gifts among people, even the rebellious,\nso that YAH God might dwell there.|Received not gave; retain unsettled final relation.
68:19|Blessed be the Lord, day after day;\nhe bears our burden, the God who saves us. Selah.|Unspecified bearing object supplied as burden, noted alternative.
68:20|Our God is a God of rescues;\nto the LORD, the Lord, belong escapes from death.|Retain plural deliverances and both divine names.
68:21|But God will crush his enemies’ heads,\nthe hairy crown of one who goes on in guilt.|Preserve violent scalp detail and habitual guilt.
68:22|The Lord said, “I will bring them back from Bashan;\nI will bring them back from the depths of the sea,|Object them inferred from enemies, repeated return retained.
68:23|so your foot may crush them in blood\nand your dogs’ tongues may have their portion from enemies.”|Keep pinned crush rather than wash, difficult bloody syntax noted.
68:24|They have seen your processions, God,\nthe processions of my God, my king, into the sanctuary.|Repeat procession, singular personal confession within public event.
68:25|Singers lead, musicians follow,\nwith young women beating tambourines between them.|Specific women and procession order retained.
68:26|Bless God in the assemblies—\nthe LORD, you who spring from Israel!|Source fountain/origin idiom clarified.
68:27|There is little Benjamin leading them,\nJudah’s princes with their throng,\nthe princes of Zebulun and the princes of Naphtali.|Four tribes and rare throng word retained.
68:28|Your God has commanded your strength.\nShow your strength, God, as you have acted for us.|Pinned your God not emended command O God; voice shift retained.
68:29|Because of your temple above Jerusalem,\nkings will bring you gifts.|Temple motive/location rather than invented procession route.

68:30|Rebuke the beast among the reeds,
the herd of bulls among the peoples’ calves,
trampling on pieces of silver.
He has scattered the peoples who delight in war.|Difficult participle chosen active with alternate submission noted; pinned scattered retained.
68:31|Envoys will come from Egypt;\nCush will hurry to stretch its hands to God.|Uncertain envoys noun and Cush name, no modern Ethiopia equation.
68:32|Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God;\nmake music to the Lord. Selah.|Keep global kingdom invitation.
68:33|He rides the ancient heavens, the highest heavens.\nListen! He gives voice—a mighty voice.|Preserve riding and doubled heavens/voice.
68:34|Ascribe strength to God;\nhis majesty is over Israel, his strength in the clouds.|Earth people and sky paired.
68:35|Awesome are you, God, from your sanctuaries!\nThe God of Israel gives strength and power to the people.\nBlessed be God!|Retain plural sanctuaries and closing blessing.
69:1|For the music leader. According to “Lilies.” Of David.\nSave me, God! The waters have reached my throat.|Nephesh bodily throat in drowning image and title preserved.
69:2|I sink into deep mud with nowhere to stand.\nI have entered deep waters; the current sweeps me away.|Keep unstable mud and engulfing water distinct.
69:3|I am worn out from calling; my throat is parched.\nMy eyes fail as I wait for my God.|Bodily exhaustion and waiting retained.

69:4|Those who hate me without cause outnumber the hairs on my head.\nMy treacherous enemies, bent on destroying me, are powerful.\nMust I restore what I never stole?|Keep hair count, strong enemies and unjust restitution question.
69:5|God, you know my folly;\nmy guilty deeds are not hidden from you.|Confession retained alongside innocence of accusation.

69:6|Do not let those who wait for you be ashamed because of me,
Lord, LORD of Armies.
Do not let those who seek you be disgraced because of me,
God of Israel.|Preserve repeated because of me and divine designations.
69:7|For your sake I bear reproach;\ndisgrace covers my face.|Affliction for God not merely private conflict.
69:8|I have become a stranger to my brothers,\nan outsider to my mother’s sons.|Specific male kin retained with emphatic maternal relation.
69:9|Zeal for your house has consumed me;\nthe insults of those who insult you have fallen on me.|Preserve consuming zeal and transfer of reproaches.
69:10|When I wept and fasted,\nit became another reproach against me.|Compressed weeping/fasting rendered without invented humiliation.
69:11|I put on sackcloth,\nand I became their byword.|Clothing and public ridicule.
69:12|Those sitting at the gate talk about me;\nI am the song of those drinking strong drink.|Retain civic gate and drinkers, no imposed social class.
69:13|But my prayer is to you, LORD, at a time of favor.\nGod, in your abundant faithful love,\nanswer me with your dependable salvation.|Keep favorable time and truth of salvation as dependability.
69:14|Pull me from the mud; do not let me sink.\nLet me escape those who hate me and the deep waters.|Repeat opening threat and human opponents together.
69:15|Do not let the current sweep me away,\nthe deep swallow me,\nor the pit close its mouth over me.|Three distinct swallowing dangers retained.
69:16|Answer me, LORD, for your faithful love is good;\nin your great compassion, turn toward me.|Love and compassion both ground petition.
69:17|Do not hide your face from your servant.\nI am in distress; hurry and answer!|Urgency and hidden face retained.
69:18|Come near and redeem my life;\nbecause of my enemies, ransom me.|Both redemption verbs and enemy motive.
69:19|You know my reproach, my shame, my disgrace;\nall my adversaries are before you.|Triple humiliation and divine awareness.
69:20|Reproach has broken my heart, and I am desperately ill.\nI looked for sympathy—there was none;\nfor comforters—I found no one.|Keep failed search and severe physical/emotional hurt.
69:21|They put poison in my food\nand gave me vinegar when I was thirsty.|Rosh poisonous/bitter substance not forced exact plant.
69:22|Let their own table become a trap before them,\na snare when they are at ease.|Difficult shlomim ease reading noted with recompense alternative.
69:23|Let their eyes grow dark so they cannot see;\nmake their loins tremble continually.|Preserve bodily curse rather than soften.
69:24|Pour your indignation on them;\nlet your burning anger catch them.|Two forms of divine anger retained.
69:25|Let their encampment lie desolate;\nlet no one live in their tents.|Plural tents retained not harmonized later quotation.
69:26|They pursue the one you struck\nand recount the pain of those you wounded.|Divine agency and human exploitation both explicit.
69:27|Add wrongdoing to their wrongdoing;\ndo not let them enter your righteousness.|Keep difficult cumulative guilt and exclusion, note vindication sense.
69:28|Let them be erased from the book of the living,\nnot enrolled with the righteous.|Retain registration image without afterlife-system expansion.
69:29|But I am afflicted and in pain;\nGod, let your salvation set me high.|Contrast suffering and protective height.
69:30|I will praise God’s name in song\nand magnify him with thanksgiving.|Song and thankful magnification retained.
69:31|This will please the LORD more than an ox,\nmore than a bull with horns and hooves.|Keep concrete sacrificial animal traits.
69:32|The humble will see and rejoice.\nYou who seek God, let your hearts revive!|Shift to direct audience command retained.
69:33|The LORD hears the needy\nand does not despise his prisoners.|Prisoners his, not generalized incarceration claim.
69:34|Let heaven and earth praise him,\nthe seas and everything moving in them.|Nonhuman sea creatures included.
69:35|God will save Zion and rebuild Judah’s towns;\nthey will live there and possess it.|Future community remains unspecified pronoun.
69:36|His servants’ offspring will inherit it;\nthose who love his name will dwell there.|Descendants and name-love close communal scope.
70:1|For the music leader. Of David. For remembrance.\nGod, come to rescue me!\nLORD, hurry to help me!|Title included and compressed first clause supplied come.
70:2|Let those seeking my life be ashamed and disgraced;\nlet those who delight in my harm retreat in humiliation.|Keep two hostile groups and parallel reversal.
70:3|Let those who say, “Aha! Aha!”\nturn back because of their shame.|Double taunt and turning retained.
70:4|Let all who seek you rejoice and be glad in you.\nLet those who love your salvation always say, “Great is God!”|God name kept distinct from parallel Psalm 40 LORD.
70:5|But I am afflicted and needy. God, hurry to me!\nYou are my help and my rescuer;\nLORD, do not delay.|Keep urgent address and both divine names.
71:1|In you, LORD, I take refuge;\nnever let me be put to shame.|No invented title; opening refuge retained.
71:2|In your righteousness rescue me and bring me to safety.\nBend your ear toward me and save me.|Two rescue verbs and listening image.
71:3|Be my rock, a dwelling I can always enter.\nYou have commanded my rescue,\nfor you are my crag and my fortress.|Pinned dwelling and commanded, not harmonized Psalm31.
71:4|My God, free me from the wicked man’s hand,\nfrom the grip of the unjust and ruthless.|Keep hands and violence, difficult ruthless term.
71:5|You are my hope, Lord, LORD,\nmy trust since youth.|Both divine names retained without collapsing title.
71:6|I have leaned on you since birth;\nyou brought me out of my mother’s womb.\nMy praise is always of you.|Gozi birth assistance rendering with uncertainty noted.
71:7|I have become a sign to many,\nbut you are my strong refuge.|Portent may be ominous, not automatically positive example.
71:8|Let my mouth be filled with your praise,\nwith your splendor all day long.|Mouth filled with sustained praise.
71:9|Do not cast me aside in old age;\ndo not forsake me when my strength is spent.|Aging and diminished strength explicit.
71:10|My enemies speak against me;\nthose watching for my life take counsel together,|Keep vigilance as threat to life.
71:11|saying, “God has forsaken him.\nPursue him and seize him; no one will rescue him.”|Quote enemy claim, not narrator endorsement.
71:12|God, do not stay far from me;\nmy God, hurry to help me!|Follow read hurry; repeated God retained.
71:13|Let my accusers be ashamed and consumed;\nlet those seeking my harm wrap themselves in reproach and disgrace.|Keep consumed and clothing humiliation.
71:14|But I will keep hoping\nand add still more to all your praise.|Continued hope and increasing praise.
71:15|My mouth will recount your righteousness,\nyour salvation all day long,\nthough I cannot count its deeds.|Rare counts word rendered counting not literary knowledge.
71:16|I will come with the mighty deeds of the Lord, the LORD;\nI will tell of your righteousness, yours alone.|Retain coming with deeds and exclusive praise.
71:17|God, you have taught me since youth;\nuntil now I have told of your wonders.|Lifelong teaching and testimony.
71:18|Even when I am old and gray, God, do not forsake me,\nuntil I tell the next generation of your arm,\nand all who are to come of your might.|Preserve arm and transmission across generations.
71:19|Your righteousness, God, reaches the heights.\nYou have done great things; God, who is like you?|Repeated God and incomparable deeds.
71:20|You have made me see many bitter troubles;\nyou will revive me again,\nbring me up again from the earth’s depths.|Read me in two variants rather than written us; repeated again.
71:21|Increase my honor;\nturn and comfort me.|Petition chosen from imperfect forms, comfort not prosperity gloss.
71:22|I too will thank you with the harp for your faithfulness, my God;\nI will make music to you with the lyre, Holy One of Israel.|Distinct instruments and divine title.
71:23|My lips will shout for joy when I make music to you,\nand so will my life, which you redeemed.|Mouth and whole living self praise together.
71:24|My tongue will ponder your righteousness all day,\nfor those seeking my harm are ashamed and disgraced.|Turn from threatened future to confidence in shame.
72:1|Of Solomon.\nGod, give the king your judgments,\nthe king’s son your righteousness.|Title of/for Solomon ambiguity noted; justice royal gift.
72:2|May he judge your people with righteousness\nand your afflicted ones with justice.|Royal petition not guaranteed history.
72:3|May the mountains bring peace to the people,\nand the hills bring it through righteousness.|Keep geographical personification and righteousness as the means of peace.
72:4|May he defend the afflicted among the people,\nsave the children of the needy,\nand crush the oppressor.|Children and violent crushing not generalized benevolence.
72:5|May they revere you while the sun endures,\nas long as the moon, generation after generation.|Pinned they fear you not emended king lives; referent note.
72:6|May he come down like rain on cut grass,\nlike showers watering the earth.|Gez cut grass with fleece alternative, preserve descent.
72:7|In his days may the righteous flourish\nand peace abound until the moon is no more.|Cosmic duration and righteous persons retained.
72:8|May he rule from sea to sea,\nfrom the River to earth’s ends.|River capitalized with Euphrates note, no inserted geography.
72:9|May desert dwellers bow before him\nand his enemies lick the dust.|Keep submission and degrading dust image.
72:10|May the kings of Tarshish and the coastlands bring tribute,\nthe kings of Sheba and Seba offer gifts.|Sheba/Seba not collapsed.
72:11|May all kings bow before him,\nall nations serve him.|Royal worldwide submission retained.
72:12|For he rescues the needy who cry out,\nthe afflicted who have no helper.|Reason for reign is rescue of vulnerable.
72:13|He has pity on the weak and needy\nand saves the lives of the needy.|Repeated needy preserved.
72:14|He redeems their lives from oppression and violence;\ntheir blood is precious in his eyes.|Blood value image not abstract dignity replacement.

72:15|May he live, and may gold from Sheba be given to him.\nMay prayer be made for him continually,\nand blessing offered to him all day.|Ambiguous pronouns retained, passive supplies no named donor.

72:16|May grain abound in the land, even on the mountain tops;\nmay its fruit wave like Lebanon,\nand people bloom from the city like the earth’s grass.|Rare abundance word and luxuriant city image retained.

72:17|May his name last forever,\nmay his name flourish as long as the sun.\nMay all nations bless themselves by him and call him happy.|Read flourish; reflexive blessing not automatically passive blessed.
72:18|Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel,\nwho alone does wonders.|Doxology distinguished from royal address.
72:19|Blessed be his glorious name forever;\nmay his glory fill the whole earth.\nAmen and amen.|Double amen and universal glory preserved.
72:20|The prayers of David son of Jesse are ended.|Collection colophon retained despite further David titles later.
73:1|A psalm of Asaph.\nGod is indeed good to Israel,\nto those whose hearts are pure.|Retains Israel and the heart qualification rather than emending to the upright.
73:2|But as for me, my feet had nearly slipped;\nI almost lost my footing.|Reads both qere verbs as the poet's threatened fall.
73:3|I envied the arrogant\nwhen I saw how well the wicked lived.|Connects envy to the wicked's shalom, their apparent well-being.
73:4|They suffer no pangs at death;\ntheir bodies are well fed.|Retains the written reference to their death; flags the difficult claim in a note.
73:5|They escape the hardships other people bear;\nthey are not struck down like everyone else.|Keeps the speaker's sweeping perception rather than softening it into sometimes.
73:6|So pride hangs around their necks like a necklace,\nand violence wraps them like a garment.|Preserves both wearable images and explicit violence.
73:7|Their eyes bulge from fatness;\nthe imaginings of their hearts spill over.|Keeps the bodily image instead of replacing eyes with iniquity.
73:8|They sneer and speak maliciously;\nfrom their lofty place they threaten oppression.|Makes the relation of evil speech and oppression readable.
73:9|They set their mouths against heaven,\nand their tongues roam the earth.|Retains the extravagant mouth and roaming tongue imagery.
73:10|So his people turn toward them\nand drink their water to the full.|Follows the qere turn; leaves his referent unsettled and notes the obscure water image.
73:11|They say, “How could God know?\nDoes the Most High know anything?”|Preserves the two questions and divine title.
73:12|Look at them—the wicked!\nAlways at ease, they pile up wealth.|Keeps the poet's accusing observation and accumulation.
73:13|Surely I have kept my heart pure for nothing\nand washed my hands in innocence in vain.|Makes the disillusionment explicit without treating it as the psalm's final claim.
73:14|All day long I am struck down;\nevery morning brings correction.|Retains the daily and morning repetition of affliction.
73:15|If I had said, “I will speak that way,”\nI would have betrayed the family of your children.|Keeps the turn to God and the communal consequence of speaking.
73:16|I tried to understand all this,\nbut it was too painful for me—|Preserves the unfinished movement into the sanctuary verse.
73:17|until I entered God's sanctuaries\nand understood where their lives were heading.|Retains plural sanctuaries and interprets their end without adding an afterlife scheme.
73:18|Yes, you set them on slippery ground;\nyou bring them crashing into ruin.|Connects their slippery position with the poet's near slip in verse 2.
73:19|How suddenly they are devastated!\nTerrors sweep them away and finish them.|Retains abruptness and both destruction clauses.
73:20|Like a dream when someone wakes,\nLord, when you rise, you dismiss their image.|Retains the dream and image analogy; notes the difficult when-you-rise expression.
73:21|When my heart turned bitter\nand pain pierced me deep inside,|Renders kidneys as the inner seat of pain, retaining the piercing action.
73:22|I was senseless and uncomprehending—\nlike an animal before you.|Keeps the poet's self-description rather than labeling other people beasts.
73:23|Yet I am always with you;\nyou hold my right hand.|Retains the emphatic continuing relationship and specified right hand.
73:24|You guide me with your counsel,\nand afterward you will receive me with honor.|Preserves receive and honor/glory without making the destination explicit.
73:25|Who do I have in heaven but you?\nWith you, I desire nothing on earth.|Retains paired heaven and earth and personal desire.
73:26|My body and my heart may fail,\nbut God is my heart's rock\nand my portion forever.|Keeps rock and portion as distinct images amid bodily failure.
73:27|Those far from you will perish;\nyou put an end to everyone who is unfaithful to you.|Renders the sexual infidelity metaphor as covenantal unfaithfulness, noted explicitly.

73:28|But for me, being near God is good.\nI have made the Lord, the LORD, my refuge,\nso I can tell of all your works.|Retains both divine designations and the final turn from his refuge to your works.
74:1|A maskil of Asaph.\nGod, why have you rejected us forever?\nWhy does your anger smoke against the sheep of your pasture?|Keeps the maskil label, forever protest, smoke and flock images.

74:2|Remember the community you acquired long ago,\nthe tribe you redeemed as your own possession—\nMount Zion, where you made your home.|Preserves acquisition, redemption and inheritance relationships.
74:3|Walk among these lasting ruins;\nsee all the damage the enemy has done in the sanctuary.|Turns lift your steps into a natural invitation while keeping enduring devastation.
74:4|Your enemies roared inside your meeting place;\nthey set up their own signs as signs of victory.|Preserves the repeated signs with a modest contextual clarification.
74:5|They looked like people swinging axes\nthrough a thicket of trees.|Retains the difficult visual comparison rather than inventing a named army.
74:6|And now they smash all its carved woodwork\nwith hatchets and hammers.|Follows the qere now and preserves both destructive tools.
74:7|They set your sanctuary on fire;\nthey defiled the dwelling of your name, leveling it to the ground.|Keeps fire, desecration and the name's dwelling together.
74:8|They said in their hearts, “We will crush them all.”\nThey burned every meeting place of God in the land.|Retains the obscure resolve to oppress and avoids anachronistic synagogues.
74:9|We see none of our signs.\nThere is no prophet left,\nand no one among us knows how long this will last.|Preserves signs in contrast to enemy signs and the unanswered duration.
74:10|God, how long will the foe mock you?\nWill the enemy scorn your name forever?|Keeps both duration questions addressed to God.
74:11|Why do you hold back your hand, your right hand?\nPull it from the fold of your robe and finish them!|Preserves the demanding imperative and right-hand body image.
74:12|Yet God has been my king from long ago,\nworking acts of rescue throughout the earth.|Keeps the singular my within the communal prayer and plural rescues.
74:13|You broke the sea apart by your strength;\nyou shattered the heads of the sea monsters on the waters.|Retains sea monsters and plural heads without reducing them to historical armies.
74:14|You crushed Leviathan's heads\nand gave him as food to creatures of the desert.|Retains multiheaded Leviathan; notes the uncertain desert recipients.
74:15|You split open springs and streams;\nyou dried up rivers that never ran dry.|Keeps paired provision and drying of enduring rivers.
74:16|The day is yours, and so is the night;\nyou established the light and the sun.|Retains the less specific light rather than silently replacing it with moon.
74:17|You set all the earth's boundaries;\nyou formed summer and winter.|Keeps space and seasons as paired creation acts.
74:18|Remember this, LORD: the enemy has mocked you;\na foolish people has treated your name with contempt.|Retains remember and specific name address without identifying an unstated nation.
74:19|Do not hand the life of your dove over to wild beasts;\ndo not forget the lives of your afflicted people forever.|Retains dove vulnerability and the repeated life language.
74:20|Look to your covenant,\nfor the land's dark places are full of dens of violence.|Keeps covenant as the appeal's ground and violence in hidden places.
74:21|Do not let the crushed turn back in shame;\nlet the poor and needy praise your name.|Retains both negative petition and desired praise.
74:22|Rise, God, and plead your own cause!\nRemember how fools mock you all day long.|Keeps legal contest and the all-day insult directed at God.
74:23|Do not forget the voices of your enemies,\nthe uproar of those who rise against you, always growing louder.|Maintains the final unresolved demand and rising noise.

75:1|For the music leader. “Do Not Destroy.” A psalm of Asaph. A song.\nWe thank you, God; we thank you.\nYour name is near; people tell of your wonders.|Retains all title elements, doubled thanks and the near name.
75:2|“When I choose the appointed time,\nI will judge fairly.|Marks the new divine voice without inserting a source-absent speech formula.
75:3|When the earth and everyone in it give way,\nI am the one who holds its pillars firm. Selah.|Keeps the earth's pillars and divine first-person contrast.
75:4|I say to the boastful, ‘Do not boast,’\nand to the wicked, ‘Do not lift your horn.|Retains horn as a linked power image rather than varying it away.
75:5|Do not lift your horn on high\nor speak with your neck stiff in arrogance.’”|Preserves both horn and neck images, closing the divine warning.
75:6|For exaltation comes neither from the east nor from the west,\nnor from the wilderness.|Reads harim as lifting up in the contextual wordplay; notes the mountain alternative.
75:7|God is the judge:\nhe brings one down and raises another up.|Keeps lowering and raising as the explanation of exaltation.

75:8|The LORD holds a cup in his hand,
full of foaming wine mixed with spices.
He pours it out,
and all the earth's wicked must drain it, down to the dregs.|Retains cup, mixed wine and compulsory drinking of residue.
75:9|But I will tell of this forever;\nI will sing to the God of Jacob.|Keeps the speaker's first-person declaration distinct from judgment speech.

75:10|“I will cut off every horn of the wicked,\nbut the horns of the righteous will be lifted high.”|Preserves the resumed first-person claim; notes speaker uncertainty rather than settling it silently.
76:1|For the music leader. With stringed instruments. A psalm of Asaph. A song.\nGod is known in Judah;\nhis name is great in Israel.|Retains musical instruction and Judah/Israel pairing.
76:2|His shelter is in Salem;\nhis dwelling is in Zion.|Keeps Salem as a place name and shelter distinct from dwelling.
76:3|There he shattered the bow's fiery arrows,\nthe shield, the sword, the weapons of war. Selah.|Retains fiery shafts and the full weapon list.
76:4|You shine with light, more majestic\nthan mountains rich with prey.|Preserves the pinned mountains of prey rather than emending to everlasting mountains.
76:5|The stouthearted have been stripped bare;\nthey have sunk into sleep.\nNone of the warriors can lift a hand.|Keeps plundering, sleep and disabled hands without euphemizing defeat.
76:6|At your rebuke, God of Jacob,\nchariot and horse lie in deep sleep.|Retains chariot rather than substituting rider and preserves the sleep image.
76:7|You—you are to be feared!\nWho can stand before you once your anger rises?|Keeps emphatic doubled you and fearful question.
76:8|You announced judgment from heaven;\nthe earth grew afraid and fell silent|Keeps silence as response to the heavenly verdict and continues the sentence.
76:9|when God rose to judge,\nto save all the afflicted of the earth. Selah.|Retains the rescue purpose and worldwide afflicted.
76:10|Even human rage will praise you;\nyou wrap yourself in the rage that remains.|Retains the difficult girding image; notes alternative restraint reading.
76:11|Make vows to the LORD your God and fulfill them;\nlet everyone around him bring gifts to the One to be feared.|Preserves fulfillment and the fearful title rather than weakening it to respect.
76:12|He cuts off the spirit of rulers;\nhe fills the kings of the earth with fear.|Keeps spirit/breath ambiguity and the final political scope.

77:1|For the music leader. According to Jeduthun. Of Asaph. A psalm.\nI cry aloud to God;\naloud I call to God, and he listens to me.|Preserves the repeated voice, qere title name and positive hearing clause.
77:2|In my distress I sought the Lord.\nAll night my hand stayed stretched out without tiring;\nI refused to be comforted.|Keeps the extended hand as prayer gesture and the refusal of comfort.
77:3|I remember God and groan;\nI reflect, and my spirit grows faint. Selah.|Retains remembering as initially painful rather than immediately consoling.
77:4|You hold my eyelids open.\nI am so troubled that I cannot speak.|Keeps direct divine agency in the sleeplessness.
77:5|I think about the days long past,\nthe years of ancient times.|Maintains paired days and years of recollection.
77:6|At night I remember my song;\nI ponder in my heart, and my spirit searches:|Preserves my song and the inner search leading to questions.
77:7|“Will the Lord reject us forever?\nWill he never show favor again?|Keeps the extreme temporal questions as the poet's lament.
77:8|Has his faithful love vanished for good?\nHas his promise failed for every generation?|Retains love and promise as separate grounds of doubt.
77:9|Has God forgotten to be gracious?\nHas anger shut away his compassion?” Selah.|Preserves the provocative questions without answering them within the verse.
77:10|Then I said, “This is what wounds me:\nthe right hand of the Most High has changed.”|Chooses the painful-change reading of difficult shenot and halloti; notes the years/appeal alternative.
77:11|I will remember the deeds of YAH;\nyes, I will remember your wonders of long ago.|Follows qere remember, retains YAH and the shift to your.
77:12|I will ponder everything you have done\nand reflect on your great deeds.|Keeps both forms of sustained remembering.
77:13|God, your way is holy.\nWhat god is as great as God?|Retains holiness and the comparative divine question.
77:14|You are the God who works wonders;\nyou have made your strength known among the peoples.|Keeps wonders and public revelation distinct.
77:15|With your arm you redeemed your people,\nthe children of Jacob and Joseph. Selah.|Preserves both ancestral names and redemption's arm image.
77:16|The waters saw you, God;\nthe waters saw you and writhed.\nEven the depths trembled.|Maintains repeated seeing and personified cosmic waters.
77:17|Clouds poured down water;\nthe skies gave their thunderous cry,\nand your arrows flashed back and forth.|Keeps arrows as the lightning image without replacing it completely.
77:18|Your thunder rolled in the whirlwind;\nlightning lit the world.\nThe earth trembled and shook.|Reads galgal as whirling storm, with the double earth reaction intact.
77:19|Your way ran through the sea,\nyour path through mighty waters,\nbut your footprints could not be found.|Follows qere singular path and retains unknowable footprints.
77:20|You led your people like a flock\nby the hands of Moses and Aaron.|Keeps both human leaders and the abrupt quiet shepherd conclusion.
78:1|A maskil of Asaph.\nMy people, listen to my instruction;\nturn your ears toward the words I speak.|Keeps the teacher's first-person instruction and direct audience.
78:2|I will open my mouth with a parable;\nI will bring forth riddles from long ago—|Preserves mashal and riddles as the framing of history.
78:3|things we have heard and known,\nthings our fathers told us.|Keeps transmission through fathers and repeated things.

78:4|We will not hide them from their children.\nWe will tell the coming generation the LORD's praiseworthy deeds,\nhis strength and the wonders he has done.|Retains their children and explicit intergenerational purpose.

78:5|He established a testimony in Jacob\nand set instruction in Israel.\nHe commanded our fathers to teach these things to their children,|Preserves testimony/instruction pairing and parental obligation.
78:6|so the next generation would know—\nchildren yet to be born—\nand rise to tell their own children.|Retains unborn children and the continuing chain of telling.
78:7|Then they would put their confidence in God,\nremember God's deeds\nand keep his commands.|Keeps confidence, memory and obedience as three linked outcomes.

78:8|They would not be like their fathers,
a stubborn, rebellious generation,
whose hearts were not steadfast
and whose spirits were not faithful to God.|Preserves both heart and spirit diagnoses without importing ethnic generalizations.
78:9|The men of Ephraim, armed with bows,\nturned back on the day of battle.|Keeps the named tribe and reversal without inventing a battle identification.
78:10|They did not keep God's covenant;\nthey refused to walk in his instruction.|Retains covenant and the walking image.
78:11|They forgot his deeds\nand the wonders he had shown them.|Preserves the memory failure as the narrative's recurring charge.
78:12|He worked wonders before their fathers\nin the land of Egypt, in the fields of Zoan.|Keeps both geographic designations.
78:13|He split the sea and led them through;\nhe made the waters stand like a heap.|Retains the piled-water image rather than making a new architectural image.
78:14|He guided them with a cloud by day\nand with the light of fire all night.|Keeps the all-night duration and day/night pairing.
78:15|He split rocks in the wilderness\nand gave them abundant water, as from the depths.|Preserves plural rocks and depths as the scale of water provision.
78:16|He brought streams out of a crag\nand made water pour down like rivers.|Retains the crag and the descending river simile.
78:17|Still they kept sinning against him,\nrebelling against the Most High in the dry land.|Keeps persistence and the divine title.
78:18|They tested God in their hearts\nby demanding food for their appetites.|Reads nephesh contextually as appetite, with intentional testing retained.
78:19|They spoke against God, saying,\n“Can God set a table in the wilderness?|Preserves the table image and challenging question.

78:20|He struck the rock, and water gushed out;
streams overflowed.
But can he also give bread?
Can he provide meat for his people?”|Keeps their admission of one miracle within their renewed challenge.
78:21|The LORD heard and was furious.\nFire flared against Jacob;\nanger rose against Israel,|Preserves anger and fire directed at the named people.
78:22|because they did not trust God\nor rely on his saving power.|Keeps trust and reliance as the reason for judgment.
78:23|Yet he commanded the skies above\nand opened heaven's doors.|Preserves cosmic doors and the contrast of continued provision.
78:24|He rained manna down for them to eat\nand gave them the grain of heaven.|Retains manna and grain as related but distinct terms.
78:25|Human beings ate the bread of mighty ones;\nhe sent food until they had enough.|Keeps mighty ones rather than specifying angels without a note.
78:26|He stirred up the east wind in the heavens\nand drove the south wind by his strength.|Preserves both compass directions.
78:27|He rained meat on them like dust,\nwinged birds like sand beside the seas.|Retains both abundance similes and unspecified birds.
78:28|He made them fall inside his camp,\nall around his dwellings.|Keeps the source's singular possessive rather than silently harmonizing to their.
78:29|They ate and were thoroughly satisfied;\nhe gave them what they craved.|Retains satisfaction preceding judgment.
78:30|But before their craving had left them,\nwhile the food was still in their mouths,|Keeps simultaneous desire and eating, leading into divine anger.
78:31|God's anger rose against them.\nHe killed their strongest men\nand struck down Israel's young men.|Preserves lethal action and the specific younger males.
78:32|Despite all this, they kept sinning;\ndespite his wonders, they did not trust.|Retains the emphatic double failure.
78:33|So he brought their days to an end like a breath,\nand their years in sudden terror.|Keeps breath/transience and alarm without assigning a lifespan.
78:34|When he killed them, they sought him;\nthey returned and searched earnestly for God.|Preserves death as the occasion of the survivors' turning.
78:35|They remembered that God was their rock,\nthat God Most High was their redeemer.|Retains rock, divine title and redeemer.
78:36|But they tried to flatter him with their mouths\nand lied to him with their tongues.|Keeps mouth/tongue parallelism and deceptive religious speech.
78:37|Their hearts were not steadfast toward him;\nthey were not faithful to his covenant.|Links steadfast hearts to the earlier generation warning.

78:38|Yet he was compassionate:
he made atonement for their wrongdoing instead of destroying them.
Again and again he turned back his anger
and did not unleash all his fury.|Retains atonement, restraint and repeated mercy without erasing judgment.
78:39|He remembered that they were only flesh,\na passing wind that does not return.|Keeps flesh and wind as human fragility images.
78:40|How often they rebelled against him in the wilderness\nand grieved him in the desert!|Retains divine grief as well as human rebellion.
78:41|Again and again they tested God\nand pained the Holy One of Israel.|Chooses pained for the difficult verb, preserving the specific divine title.
78:42|They did not remember his hand,\nthe day he redeemed them from the foe,|Keeps hand as power image and introduces retrospective rescue.
78:43|when he displayed his signs in Egypt\nand his wonders in the fields of Zoan.|Preserves the repeated geography and signs/wonders pairing.
78:44|He turned their rivers to blood;\nthey could not drink from their streams.|Retains plural watercourses rather than naming only the Nile.
78:45|He sent swarms of flies that devoured them\nand frogs that brought them ruin.|Keeps the poem's order and destructive hyperbole.
78:46|He gave their crops to the devouring locust,\nthe fruit of their labor to the swarming locust.|Preserves two locust terms and their agricultural losses.
78:47|He killed their vines with hail\nand their sycamore figs with frost.|Keeps frost as a qualified reading of the rare destructive-weather term.
78:48|He handed their cattle over to hail,\ntheir livestock to bolts of fire.|Preserves hail and fiery bolts without harmonizing the list to Exodus.

78:49|He sent his burning anger against them—\nfury, indignation and distress—\na company of messengers bringing disaster.|Retains the wrath list and harmful messengers without making them morally evil spirits.
78:50|He cleared a path for his anger.\nHe did not spare their lives from death\nbut handed them over to plague.|Keeps the path image and explicit lethal agency.
78:51|He struck every firstborn in Egypt,\nthe first fruits of their strength in the tents of Ham.|Preserves firstborn, reproductive strength and ancestral designation Ham.
78:52|Then he brought his people out like sheep\nand guided them like a flock through the wilderness.|Retains paired shepherd images.
78:53|He led them safely, so they were not afraid,\nbut the sea covered their enemies.|Keeps the contrast of safety and drowning without adding detail.
78:54|He brought them to his holy territory,\nto this mountain his right hand had acquired.|Preserves mountain and right-hand acquisition.

78:55|He drove nations out before them,\nallotted their land as an inheritance by measuring line,\nand settled Israel's tribes in their tents.|Keeps dispossession, allocation and occupied dwellings explicit.
78:56|But they tested God Most High and rebelled against him;\nthey did not keep his testimonies.|Preserves the renewed failure after settlement.
78:57|They turned away and acted treacherously like their fathers;\nthey twisted aside like an unreliable bow.|Keeps the defective bow metaphor and ancestral comparison.
78:58|They angered him with their high places\nand provoked his jealousy with their carved images.|Retains cultic high places and jealousy rather than reducing both to generic wrongdoing.
78:59|God heard and was furious;\nhe utterly rejected Israel.|Preserves the severe rejection claim without treating it as the poem's final word.
78:60|He abandoned his dwelling at Shiloh,\nthe tent where he had lived among human beings.|Keeps the site and divine dwelling among people.
78:61|He gave his strength into captivity,\nhis splendor into the enemy's hand.|Retains the metaphorical strength/splendor language; notes the ark association.
78:62|He handed his people over to the sword;\nhe was furious with his own inheritance.|Keeps violent judgment and inheritance as his people.
78:63|Fire consumed their young men,\nand their young women had no wedding songs.|Retains gender-specific losses and the suppressed marriage celebration.
78:64|Their priests fell by the sword,\nand their widows did not weep.|Keeps absent mourning without inventing a reason.
78:65|Then the Lord awoke as though from sleep,\nlike a warrior shouting after wine.|Preserves the striking wine and awakening simile without sanitizing it.
78:66|He struck his enemies from behind\nand put them to lasting shame.|Retains the ambiguous rearward blow and lasting disgrace.
78:67|He rejected Joseph's tent\nand did not choose the tribe of Ephraim.|Keeps Joseph and Ephraim distinct within the contrast.
78:68|Instead he chose the tribe of Judah,\nMount Zion, which he loved.|Preserves the two objects of choice and love.
78:69|He built his sanctuary like the heights,\nlike the earth he established forever.|Retains heights rather than specifying mountains absent from this noun.
78:70|He chose David his servant\nand took him from the sheepfolds.|Keeps David's election and humble shepherd setting.
78:71|From tending nursing ewes he brought him\nto shepherd Jacob his people,\nIsrael his inheritance.|Preserves nursing sheep and the transfer to human shepherding.
78:72|He shepherded them with an undivided heart\nand guided them with skillful hands.|Retains heart integrity and hand skill as the concluding pair.

79:1|A psalm of Asaph.
God, nations have invaded your inheritance.
They have defiled your holy temple
and reduced Jerusalem to rubble.|Retains all three dimensions of invasion, desecration and destruction.
79:2|They have given your servants' corpses to the birds of the sky for food,\nthe flesh of your faithful people to the beasts of the earth.|Preserves the unburied bodies and physical violence.
79:3|They have poured out their blood like water around Jerusalem,\nand no one is left to bury them.|Keeps blood/water comparison and missing burial.
79:4|Our neighbors treat us with contempt;\nthose around us mock and jeer.|Retains the surrounding community's ridicule.
79:5|How long, LORD? Will you be angry forever?\nWill your jealousy keep burning like fire?|Preserves duration questions and jealousy as fire.
79:6|Pour out your fury on the nations that do not know you,\non kingdoms that do not call on your name.|Keeps the requested redirection of divine wrath explicit.
79:7|For they have devoured Jacob\nand devastated his home.|Renders the collective foes naturally while retaining the devouring metaphor.

79:8|Do not hold past wrongs against us.\nLet your compassion hurry to meet us,\nfor we have been brought very low.|Leaves past/ancestral wrongdoing scope open in note and preserves urgent compassion.

79:9|Help us, God our savior,
for the glory of your name.
Rescue us and make atonement for our sins,
for the sake of your name.|Keeps doubled name appeal and atonement term.
79:10|Why should the nations ask, “Where is their God?”\nBefore our eyes, let the nations see\nyou avenge your servants' spilled blood.|Preserves the requested visible vengeance and qere nations.
79:11|Let the prisoner's groan reach you.\nBy the strength of your mighty arm,\nkeep alive those marked for death.|Retains prisoner, arm and threatened lives without changing them to metaphors.
79:12|Lord, pay our neighbors back sevenfold,\nright into their laps,\nfor the contempt they have shown you.|Preserves exact sevenfold retaliation and lap image.
79:13|Then we, your people, the sheep of your pasture,\nwill thank you forever.\nGeneration after generation, we will tell of your praise.|Keeps flock identity and intergenerational praise promise.

80:1|For the music leader. “Lilies.” A testimony. Of Asaph. A psalm.
Shepherd of Israel, listen—
you who lead Joseph like a flock!
You who sit enthroned above the cherubim, shine forth!|Preserves the title's uncertain musical terms and shepherd/throne pairing.
80:2|Before Ephraim, Benjamin and Manasseh,\nrouse your strength\nand come to save us.|Keeps all three tribes in their order.
80:3|God, restore us;\nlet your face shine, and we will be saved.|Establishes the recurring refrain without later expanded divine titles.
80:4|LORD, God of Armies,\nhow long will your anger smoke against your people's prayer?|Preserves smoking anger specifically against prayer.
80:5|You have fed them bread made of tears\nand given them tears to drink by the measure.|Keeps tears as both food and drink and the uncertain measure rather than inventing a volume.
80:6|You have made us a cause of strife among our neighbors;\nour enemies laugh among themselves.|Keeps conflict and the source's reflexive laughter phrase.
80:7|God of Armies, restore us;\nlet your face shine, and we will be saved.|Retains the expanded refrain title with identical remaining wording.
80:8|You brought a vine out of Egypt;\nyou drove out nations and planted it.|Keeps the sustained vine image and dispossession.
80:9|You cleared a place for it;\nit took deep root and filled the land.|Retains preparation, roots and spreading growth.
80:10|Mountains lay under its shade,\nand mighty cedars beneath its branches.|Reads cedars of God as mighty while retaining the vine's immense scale.
80:11|It sent its branches as far as the sea,\nits shoots as far as the River.|Preserves the two geographic boundaries and capitalized conventional River.
80:12|Why have you broken down its walls,\nso that everyone passing by plucks its fruit?|Keeps the direct accusation and exposed fruit.
80:13|A boar from the forest tears it apart;\ncreatures of the field feed on it.|Preserves the specific boar and wider field animals.
80:14|God of Armies, please return!\nLook down from heaven and see;\ncare for this vine,|Keeps return answering restore and the request to attend the vine.
80:15|the stock your right hand planted,\nthe son you made strong for yourself.|Retains the difficult shift from plant to son and notes its ambiguity.
80:16|It is burned with fire and cut down;\nat the rebuke of your face, they perish.|Preserves the singular vine to plural they change rather than hiding it.
80:17|Let your hand rest on the man at your right hand,\nthe son of man you made strong for yourself.|Keeps man/son-of-man parallelism without settling a later identification.
80:18|Then we will not turn away from you.\nGive us life, and we will call on your name.|Retains community pledge and dependence on renewed life.
80:19|LORD, God of Armies, restore us;\nlet your face shine, and we will be saved.|Preserves the fullest divine title at the final refrain.
81:1|For the music leader. According to the Gittith. Of Asaph.\nSing out to God our strength;\nshout for joy to the God of Jacob.|Retains the uncertain Gittith label and paired praise calls.
81:2|Strike up a song and sound the tambourine,\nthe sweet lyre together with the harp.|Keeps the distinct instruments and pleasant lyre quality.
81:3|Blow the ram's horn at the new moon,\nat the full moon, on our festival day.|Retains lunar markers; notes uncertainty about keseh and festival identification.
81:4|This is a statute for Israel,\na ruling of the God of Jacob.|Preserves parallel legal descriptions.

81:5|He established it as a testimony in Joseph\nwhen he went out against the land of Egypt.\nI hear a language I did not know:|Preserves Joseph and the ambiguous departure phrase, marking the voice transition.
81:6|“I lifted the burden from his shoulder;\nhis hands were freed from the basket.|Retains the third-person laborer and concrete forced-labor objects.

81:7|You called in distress, and I rescued you.\nI answered you from thunder's hiding place;\nI tested you at the waters of Meribah. Selah.|Keeps the shift to you, thunder concealment and named test site.
81:8|Listen, my people, while I warn you.\nIsrael, if only you would listen to me!|Preserves warning and the longing conditional appeal.
81:9|There must be no strange god among you;\nyou must not bow down to a foreign god.|Keeps both prohibition clauses.
81:10|I am the LORD your God,\nwho brought you up from Egypt.\nOpen your mouth wide, and I will fill it.|Retains exodus identification and feeding promise image.
81:11|But my people did not listen to my voice;\nIsrael would have none of me.|Keeps the emphatic refusal beyond simple inattentiveness.
81:12|So I let them follow their stubborn hearts,\nto walk by their own plans.|Retains handing over to self-chosen counsel.
81:13|If only my people would listen to me,\nif only Israel would walk in my ways!|Repeats longing and walking language consistently.
81:14|I would soon subdue their enemies\nand turn my hand against their foes.|Keeps speed and the divine hand's redirected action.
81:15|Those who hate the LORD would cringe before him,\nand their time would last forever.|Preserves ambiguous their time rather than inserting punishment or prosperity as certain.

81:16|He would feed his people the finest wheat,\nand I would satisfy you with honey from the rock.”|Preserves he-to-I and people-to-you shifts; makes collective Israel explicit for the singular recipient.
82:1|A psalm of Asaph.\nGod stands in the divine assembly;\namong the gods he gives judgment:|Preserves gods and assembly rather than resolving the identity as human judges.
82:2|“How long will you judge unjustly\nand favor the wicked? Selah.|Keeps the divine rebuke and judicial partiality.
82:3|Give justice to the weak and the fatherless;\nuphold the rights of the afflicted and the poor.|Preserves the vulnerable groups and legal vindication.
82:4|Rescue the weak and the needy;\nfree them from the hand of the wicked.|Retains active rescue alongside judgment.
82:5|They neither know nor understand;\nthey walk about in darkness.\nAll the foundations of the earth are shaking.|Keeps the shift to they and cosmic consequences.
82:6|I said, ‘You are gods,\nall of you sons of the Most High.’|Retains the stated divine designations and gender-specific sons.
82:7|Yet you will die like human beings;\nyou will fall like any ruler.”|Preserves the mortality verdict without defining the judged beings in advance.
82:8|Rise, God, and judge the earth,\nfor all the nations are yours to inherit.|Keeps the community's closing appeal and inheritance of nations.
83:1|A song. A psalm of Asaph.\nGod, do not stay silent!\nDo not be deaf or still, God!|Preserves three urgent pleas rather than collapsing the repetition.
83:2|Look, your enemies are in an uproar;\nthose who hate you lift their heads.|Keeps the noise and threatening posture.
83:3|They devise cunning plans against your people;\nthey conspire against those you shelter.|Retains the protected people's identity and deliberate plotting.
83:4|“Come,” they say, “let us wipe them out as a nation,\nso Israel's name will never be remembered again.”|Preserves the explicit extermination threat and memory erasure.
83:5|They plot with a single purpose;\nthey have made a covenant against you:|Retains covenant even for the hostile alliance.
83:6|the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites,\nMoab and the Hagrites,|Keeps all four named groups and Edom's tents.
83:7|Gebal, Ammon and Amalek,\nPhilistia with the people of Tyre.|Preserves place and people distinctions without modern equivalents.
83:8|Assyria has joined them too,\nlending its arm to the descendants of Lot. Selah.|Retains the arm image and Lot's descendants.
83:9|Do to them what you did to Midian,\nto Sisera and Jabin at the Kishon stream.|Keeps the historical comparisons and named watercourse.
83:10|They were destroyed at En-dor;\nthey became manure for the ground.|Preserves the graphic corpse image.
83:11|Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb,\nall their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna,|Retains all four names and the nobles/princes parallel.
83:12|who said, “Let us take God's pastures\nas our own possession.”|Keeps pastoral territory and the enemies' claimed possession.
83:13|My God, make them like whirling tumbleweed,\nlike straw before the wind.|Chooses windblown plant for galgal and retains both lightness images.
83:14|As fire burns a forest,\nas flame sets mountains ablaze,|Preserves the spread of destructive fire.
83:15|so pursue them with your storm\nand terrify them with your whirlwind.|Keeps the direct petition for terror and pursuit.
83:16|Fill their faces with disgrace\nso that they seek your name, LORD.|Preserves seeking the name as a purpose within the curse.
83:17|Let them be ashamed and terrified forever;\nlet them be disgraced and perish.|Keeps the severe competing demand without harmonizing it to verse 16.
83:18|Let them know that you alone, whose name is the LORD,\nare Most High over all the earth.|Retains name, exclusive claim and worldwide scope.
84:1|For the music leader. According to the Gittith. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.\nHow beloved are your dwellings,\nLORD of Armies!|Keeps plural dwellings and title attribution.
84:2|I long for the LORD's courts until I grow faint;\nmy heart and my flesh cry out to the living God.|Retains the embodied longing and living divine title.

84:3|Even a bird finds a home,
and a swallow a nest for her young,
near your altars, LORD of Armies,
my king and my God.|Preserves bird/maternal nest imagery and altar proximity without asserting nests on burning altars.
84:4|How fortunate are those who live in your house!\nThey keep praising you. Selah.|Retains continuing praise and the beatitude pattern.
84:5|How fortunate are those whose strength is in you,\nwhose hearts hold the roads of pilgrimage!|Makes the contextual destination of heart-highways readable while noting the compressed Hebrew.

84:6|As they pass through the Valley of Baca,\nthey make it a place of springs;\nthe early rain clothes it with blessings.|Keeps Baca untranslated, rain and blessings, with alternative meanings noted.
84:7|They go from strength to strength;\neach appears before God in Zion.|Preserves progressive strength and the individual appearance within the group.
84:8|LORD, God of Armies, hear my prayer;\nlisten, God of Jacob. Selah.|Retains both divine titles and singular prayer.
84:9|God, look on our shield;\nlook upon the face of your anointed one.|Reads shield parallel to anointed ruler, with the divine-shield alternative noted.

84:10|One day in your courts is better than a thousand.\nI would rather stand at the threshold of my God's house\nthan live in the tents of wickedness.|Retains exact thousand and threshold without inventing an official doorkeeper position.

84:11|For the LORD God is a sun and a shield;
the LORD gives favor and honor.
He holds back nothing good
from those who walk with integrity.|Preserves sun, shield, gifts and moral qualification.
84:12|LORD of Armies,\nhow fortunate is the one who trusts in you!|Closes with the third beatitude and personal trust.

85:1|For the music leader. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.\nLORD, you showed favor to your land;\nyou restored Jacob's fortunes.|Follows the restoration idiom while retaining its possible captivity association in a note.
85:2|You lifted away your people's guilt;\nyou covered all their sin. Selah.|Keeps lifting and covering as distinct forgiveness images.
85:3|You withdrew all your fury\nand turned away from your burning anger.|Retains total withdrawal and burning anger.
85:4|Restore us, God our savior;\nput an end to your anger toward us.|Keeps the move from remembered restoration to present need.
85:5|Will you be angry with us forever?\nWill your anger stretch from generation to generation?|Preserves the repeated question across generations.
85:6|Will you not give us life again,\nso your people can rejoice in you?|Retains revived life as the ground of joy.
85:7|Show us your faithful love, LORD;\ngrant us your salvation.|Keeps paired love and rescue petitions.

85:8|Let me hear what God the LORD will say.\nHe will speak peace to his people, his faithful ones—\nbut let them not turn back to folly.|Preserves the singular listening voice and the condition on promised peace.
85:9|Surely his salvation is near those who fear him,\nso that glory may dwell in our land.|Keeps fear and indwelling glory rather than reducing glory to prosperity.
85:10|Faithful love and faithfulness meet;\nrighteousness and peace kiss.|Preserves the four personifications and their bodily encounter.
85:11|Faithfulness sprouts from the earth,\nand righteousness looks down from heaven.|Keeps the earth/heaven movements of the personifications.
85:12|The LORD will indeed give what is good,\nand our land will yield its harvest.|Retains material harvest within the larger restoration.
85:13|Righteousness will walk ahead of him\nand make a way for his footsteps.|Reads righteousness as preparing the route; notes the difficult final clause.
86:1|A prayer of David.\nLean down and listen, LORD; answer me,\nfor I am poor and needy.|Retains the ear-inclining appeal and concrete need.
86:2|Guard my life, for I am faithful to you.\nYou are my God; save your servant who trusts in you.|Keeps the fidelity claim, servant identity and direct trust.
86:3|Be gracious to me, Lord,\nfor I call to you all day long.|Retains Adonai as Lord and persistent calling.
86:4|Bring joy to your servant's life,\nfor I lift my life to you, Lord.|Keeps the repeated nephesh connection and lifting image.
86:5|For you, Lord, are good and ready to forgive,\nrich in faithful love toward everyone who calls to you.|Retains forgiveness and universal scope of the invitation.
86:6|LORD, listen to my prayer;\npay attention to my pleas for mercy.|Preserves the doubled hearing request.
86:7|When distress comes, I call to you,\nbecause you answer me.|Keeps confident answer as the reason for prayer.
86:8|Among the gods there is none like you, Lord;\nno deeds compare with yours.|Preserves the comparison among gods without doctrinal replacement.
86:9|All the nations you made will come\nand bow before you, Lord;\nthey will honor your name.|Keeps nations as created communities and their worship.
86:10|For you are great and work wonders;\nyou alone are God.|Retains the exclusive declaration alongside verse 8's comparison.
86:11|Teach me your way, LORD,\nso I may walk in your truth.\nGive me an undivided heart to fear your name.|Keeps way, walking, truth and united-heart petition.
86:12|Lord my God, I will thank you with all my heart\nand honor your name forever.|Connects whole-heart praise to the preceding petition.
86:13|For your faithful love toward me is great;\nyou have rescued my life from the depths of Sheol.|Retains Sheol without equating it with final punishment.
86:14|God, arrogant people have risen against me;\na gang of ruthless men is seeking my life.\nThey give no thought to you.|Keeps collective deadly hostility and neglect of God.
86:15|But you, Lord, are a compassionate and gracious God,\nslow to anger and rich in faithful love and faithfulness.|Preserves the recognizable mercy formula and both faithfulness terms.
86:16|Turn toward me and be gracious.\nGive your strength to your servant;\nsave the son of your servant woman.|Keeps the maternal servant relationship rather than removing its social language.

86:17|Show me a sign of your goodness,\nso those who hate me may see it and be ashamed,\nbecause you, LORD, have helped and comforted me.|Retains visible sign, opponents' shame and concluding assurance.
87:1|Of the sons of Korah. A psalm. A song.\nThe city he founded stands on the holy mountains.|Makes the founded city explicit from the Zion context while retaining its holy-mountain setting.
87:2|The LORD loves Zion's gates\nmore than all the dwellings of Jacob.|Keeps the explicit comparison and city gates.
87:3|Glorious things are spoken of you,\ncity of God. Selah.|Retains the direct address to the city.
87:4|“I count Rahab and Babylon among those who know me.\nLook: Philistia, Tyre and Cush—\n‘This one was born there.’”|Keeps all nations, divine voice and ambiguous there; explains Rahab in note.
87:5|Of Zion it will be said,\n“This one and that one were born in her,”\nand the Most High himself will establish her.|Retains individual inclusion and the city's feminine personification.
87:6|When the LORD records the peoples, he counts,\n“This one was born there.” Selah.|Keeps the birth-register image and repeated wording.
87:7|Singers and dancers say,\n“All my springs are in you.”|Preserves springs rather than reducing the image to happiness; notes possible pipers.

88:1|A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah. For the music leader. According to Mahalath Leannoth. A maskil of Heman the Ezrahite.\nLORD, God of my salvation,\nI cry out by day and stand before you at night.|Preserves the full difficult title and the day/night prayer sequence.
88:2|Let my prayer come before you;\nlean down and hear my cry.|Keeps approach and hearing petitions.
88:3|My life is filled with troubles;\nI have come to the edge of Sheol.|Retains saturation with trouble and the named realm of death.
88:4|I am counted among those going down to the pit;\nI am like a man with no strength left.|Keeps the social reckoning among the dying.

88:5|I am set apart among the dead,
like the slain lying in a grave,
whom you remember no more,
cut off from your hand.|Preserves the anguished claim of divine forgetting and ambiguous freedom/separation among the dead.
88:6|You have put me in the lowest pit,\nin dark places, in the depths.|Retains explicit divine agency and layered descent.
88:7|Your fury presses heavily on me;\nyou overwhelm me with all your breakers. Selah.|Keeps pressure and sea-wave images.
88:8|You have driven my companions far away\nand made me repulsive to them.\nI am shut in, with no way out.|Preserves social rejection, revulsion and confinement.
88:9|My eyes waste away with affliction.\nEvery day I call to you, LORD;\nI spread my hands toward you.|Keeps bodily decline and persistent prayer gesture.
88:10|Do you work wonders for the dead?\nDo the shades rise up and thank you? Selah.|Retains shades and unanswered questions rather than inserting later resurrection conclusions.
88:11|Is your faithful love recounted in the grave,\nyour faithfulness in Abaddon?|Keeps grave and Abaddon as paired death-world terms.
88:12|Are your wonders known in the darkness,\nyour righteousness in the land of oblivion?|Preserves the location of forgetting and the repeated question structure.
88:13|But I cry to you for help, LORD;\nin the morning my prayer comes to meet you.|Keeps the persistent turn despite absent relief.
88:14|Why, LORD, do you reject me?\nWhy do you hide your face from me?|Retains the direct questions without adding reassurance.
88:15|From my youth I have been afflicted and near death;\nI bear your terrors and am overwhelmed.|Keeps lifelong suffering; notes the rare final verb's uncertainty.
88:16|Your burning anger has swept over me;\nyour terrors have destroyed me.|Preserves the speaker's extreme claim and divine possessives.
88:17|All day they surround me like water;\nthey close in on me from every side.|Retains surrounding flood as the action of terrors.
88:18|You have driven lover and friend far from me;\nmy companions are darkness.|Keeps the abrupt final darkness without supplying a hopeful ending.

89:1|A maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite.\nI will sing of the LORD's faithful love forever;\nwith my mouth I will make your faithfulness known to every generation.|Preserves title, lasting love and direct-address transition.
89:2|For I said, “Faithful love is built to last forever;\nyou establish your faithfulness in the heavens.”|Keeps I said as pinned and the building image.
89:3|“I have made a covenant with my chosen one;\nI have sworn to David my servant:|Marks the divine voice and both covenant and oath.
89:4|‘I will establish your offspring forever\nand build your throne for every generation.’” Selah.|Preserves dynastic offspring and throne-building repetition.
89:5|The heavens praise your wonders, LORD,\nyour faithfulness in the assembly of holy ones.|Keeps the heavenly assembly and faithfulness theme.
89:6|Who in the skies can compare with the LORD?\nWho among the sons of gods is like the LORD?|Retains the unusual divine-sons designation and both occurrences of the name.
89:7|God is greatly feared in the council of holy ones,\nmore awesome than all who surround him.|Keeps divine council imagery and comparative awe.
89:8|LORD, God of Armies, who is mighty like you, YAH?\nYour faithfulness surrounds you.|Preserves both full and short divine names and surrounding faithfulness.
89:9|You rule the sea's raging pride;\nwhen its waves rise, you still them.|Keeps pride/raging sense and calming action.
89:10|You crushed Rahab like a slain warrior;\nwith your strong arm you scattered your enemies.|Retains mythic Rahab and the slain comparison, with an explanatory note.
89:11|The heavens are yours; the earth is yours too.\nYou founded the world and everything in it.|Preserves ownership and founding as distinct assertions.
89:12|You created north and south;\nTabor and Hermon shout for joy at your name.|Keeps directions and both named mountains.
89:13|Your arm is mighty;\nyour hand is strong, your right hand raised high.|Retains the three-part bodily power imagery.
89:14|Righteousness and justice are your throne's foundation;\nfaithful love and faithfulness go before you.|Preserves all four qualities as structural and processional images.
89:15|How fortunate are the people who know the shout of celebration!\nLORD, they walk in the light of your face.|Keeps festival acclamation and face-light walking.
89:16|They rejoice in your name all day long\nand are lifted high by your righteousness.|Retains the sustained joy and raising action.
89:17|For you are the splendor of their strength;\nby your favor our horn is lifted high.|Follows qere passive rise and preserves their/our shift and horn.
89:18|Our shield belongs to the LORD,\nour king to the Holy One of Israel.|Keeps the king parallel explaining the shield metaphor.

89:19|Then you spoke in a vision to your faithful ones:\n“I have given help to a warrior;\nI have raised up a chosen man from the people.|Retains plural faithful ones in the pinned text and the divine announcement.
89:20|I have found David my servant;\nI have anointed him with my holy oil.|Keeps finding and anointing with concrete oil.
89:21|My hand will remain firm with him;\nmy arm will strengthen him.|Preserves hand and arm as separate parallel clauses.
89:22|No enemy will exact tribute from him;\nno wicked man will oppress him.|Chooses the creditor/oppressor sense of yashi while noting outwitting as an alternative.
89:23|I will crush his foes before him\nand strike down those who hate him.|Keeps the explicit violence of the royal promise.
89:24|My faithfulness and faithful love will be with him;\nthrough my name his horn will be lifted high.|Preserves repeated covenant attributes and horn image.
89:25|I will set his hand over the sea,\nhis right hand over the rivers.|Retains geographical scope through bodily imagery without adding borders.
89:26|He will call to me, ‘You are my father,\nmy God, the rock of my salvation.’|Keeps royal sonship and rock title together.
89:27|I will make him my firstborn,\nthe highest of the kings of the earth.|Retains bestowed rank rather than suggesting biological birth order.
89:28|I will keep my faithful love for him forever;\nmy covenant with him will stand firm.|Follows qere keep with enduring covenant assurance.
89:29|I will establish his offspring for all time,\nhis throne as long as the heavens endure.|Keeps offspring and throne with cosmic duration.
89:30|If his sons abandon my instruction\nand do not walk by my rulings,|Retains specific royal sons and conditional structure.
89:31|if they profane my statutes\nand do not keep my commands,|Preserves the second conditional pair rather than compressing repetition.
89:32|I will punish their rebellion with a rod\nand their wrongdoing with blows.|Keeps corporeal punishment and moral distinctions.
89:33|But I will not withdraw my faithful love from him\nor betray my faithfulness.|Retains the shift from sons to him and the covenant limitation on punishment.
89:34|I will not profane my covenant\nor change what my lips have spoken.|Preserves profanation echo and spoken commitment.
89:35|Once for all I have sworn by my holiness;\nI will not lie to David.|Renders the Hebrew oath idiom as a firm negative, not a conditional possibility.
89:36|His offspring will last forever,\nand his throne will be like the sun before me.|Keeps solar comparison and divine presence.
89:37|Like the moon it will be established forever,\na faithful witness in the skies.” Selah.|Preserves lunar witness imagery, noting the witness's possible distinct identity.
89:38|But you have rejected and spurned him;\nyou have been furious with your anointed one.|Keeps the sharp protest against the preceding promise.
89:39|You have renounced your servant's covenant;\nyou have defiled his crown in the dust.|Retains the accusation of covenant repudiation without explaining it away.
89:40|You have broken down all his walls\nand reduced his fortresses to ruins.|Keeps defensive structures and total damage.
89:41|Everyone passing by plunders him;\nhe has become a disgrace to his neighbors.|Retains ongoing vulnerability and local contempt.
89:42|You have raised his enemies' right hand\nand made all his foes rejoice.|Keeps divine agency in the enemy's advantage.
89:43|You have turned back the edge of his sword\nand have not sustained him in battle.|Preserves military defeat and withheld support.
89:44|You have put an end to his splendor\nand hurled his throne to the ground.|Chooses splendor for the difficult purity/brightness term with a note.
89:45|You have cut short the days of his youth\nand wrapped him in shame. Selah.|Retains shortened youth and shame as a garment.
89:46|How long, LORD? Will you hide forever?\nWill your fury keep burning like fire?|Preserves unanswered duration questions and fire image.
89:47|Remember how brief my life is.\nWhy have you created all human beings for such futility?|Keeps first-person mortality and the searching creation question.
89:48|What man can live without seeing death?\nWho can rescue his life from the hand of Sheol? Selah.|Retains death sight and Sheol's grasp as distinct images.
89:49|Lord, where is your former faithful love,\nwhich in your faithfulness you swore to David?|Keeps the concluding appeal to oath and past love.

89:50|Remember, Lord, the disgrace your servants bear,\nhow I carry in my breast the taunts of all the many peoples,|Renders the compressed final clause with implied taunts from the context; marks the difficulty.
89:51|the taunts of your enemies, LORD,\nwho mock every step of your anointed one.|Retains footsteps rather than rewriting them as delayed messianic arrival.
89:52|Blessed be the LORD forever.\nAmen and amen.|Preserves the book-closing doxology and doubled amen amid unresolved lament.
90:1|A prayer of Moses, the man of God.\nLord, you have been our dwelling place\nfrom generation to generation.|Retains title attribution and home image across generations.
90:2|Before the mountains were born,\nbefore you brought forth the earth and the world,\nfrom eternity to eternity, you are God.|Preserves the birth imagery and God's unbounded duration.
90:3|You turn human beings back to dust\nand say, “Return, children of humanity.”|Renders crushed material as dust with a note and preserves the double return.
90:4|A thousand years in your sight\nare like yesterday once it has passed,\nlike a watch in the night.|Keeps exact thousand and both time comparisons without conversion formulas.
90:5|You sweep them away; they are like sleep,\nlike grass that springs up in the morning.|Preserves flooding away, sleep and fresh grass images.
90:6|In the morning it blooms and grows;\nby evening it withers and dries up.|Keeps the day-length contrast and both final decay verbs.
90:7|Your anger consumes us;\nyour fury leaves us terrified.|Retains the communal confession under divine anger.
90:8|You have set our wrongs before you,\nour hidden sins in the light of your face.|Follows qere set; keeps illumination of what is hidden.
90:9|All our days pass under your wrath;\nwe finish our years like a sigh.|Preserves lifespan and sigh rather than a developed-life narrative.

90:10|Our years amount to seventy,
or eighty if we have the strength.
Yet all they boast of is toil and sorrow;
they pass quickly, and we fly away.|Keeps exact ages, limited strength and the flight image.
90:11|Who understands the strength of your anger,\nyour fury in keeping with the fear you deserve?|Retains the difficult relation between wrath and fear without redefining fear as mere respect.
