90:12|Teach us to count our days rightly,\nso we may gain a heart of wisdom.|Keeps counting as the route to wise-hearted living.
90:13|Return, LORD! How long?\nHave compassion on your servants.|Preserves the reversal of return language and urgent unfinished question.
90:14|Satisfy us in the morning with your faithful love,\nso we may sing for joy and be glad all our days.|Keeps morning answer to mortality and all-days joy.
90:15|Give us as many days of joy as days you afflicted us,\nas many years as we have known trouble.|Retains the proportional request and explicit divine affliction.
90:16|Let your servants see your work,\nand their children your splendor.|Keeps work and splendor with intergenerational extension.
90:17|May the favor of the Lord our God rest on us.\nEstablish the work of our hands for us—\nyes, establish the work of our hands.|Retains the deliberate full closing repetition.
91:1|Whoever dwells in the shelter of the Most High\nwill spend the night in Shaddai's shadow.|Keeps dwelling/night lodging and transliterated divine title.
91:2|I say to the LORD, “My refuge and my fortress,\nmy God, in whom I trust.”|Preserves pinned first-person I say rather than harmonizing to you say.
91:3|He will rescue you from the bird-catcher's snare\nand from deadly plague.|Retains trap and disease as distinct dangers.

91:10|no harm will meet you,\nno plague will come near your tent.|Keeps paired assurances and the concrete tent.
91:11|For he will command his angels concerning you,\nto guard you in all your ways.|Retains all your ways and angels as the commanded agents.
91:12|They will carry you on their hands,\nso you do not strike your foot against a stone.|Keeps hand and foot specificity.
91:13|You will tread on lion and cobra;\nyou will trample young lion and serpent.|Retains four animal terms, with tannin uncertainty explained in vocabulary.
91:14|“Because he clings to me in love, I will free him;\nI will set him safely on high, because he knows my name.|Marks the divine voice and retains attachment, elevation and known name.
91:15|He will call to me, and I will answer.\nI will be with him in distress;\nI will rescue him and honor him.|Preserves actual distress within the psalm's strong protection claims.
91:16|I will satisfy him with a long life\nand let him see my salvation.”|Keeps length of life and experienced salvation without adding immortality.
92:1|A psalm. A song for the Sabbath day.\nIt is good to thank the LORD\nand sing to your name, Most High,|Preserves the Sabbath title and shift to direct address.
92:2|to tell of your faithful love in the morning\nand your faithfulness through the nights,|Keeps morning and plural nights, with love/faithfulness distinction.
92:3|with the ten-stringed instrument and the harp,\nwith music resounding on the lyre.|Preserves the instrument list while avoiding a precise unsupported musical reconstruction.
92:4|For your work has made me glad, LORD;\nat the works of your hands I shout for joy.|Keeps divine work and hands as grounds of joy.
92:5|How great your works are, LORD!\nHow very deep your thoughts!|Preserves the paired exclamations and depth image.
92:6|A senseless person does not know;\na fool cannot understand this:|Introduces the following paradox rather than treating this as a general insult.
92:7|though the wicked sprout like grass\nand all who do wrong flourish,\nit is only for them to be destroyed forever.|Keeps apparent flourishing and its severe stated outcome.

92:9|Look, your enemies, LORD—\nlook, your enemies will perish!\nAll who do wrong will be scattered.|Preserves the emphatic repeated opening.
92:10|You have raised my horn like a wild ox's;\nI am refreshed with fresh oil.|Keeps horn, wild ox and oil; notes uncertainty in the oil verb.

92:12|The righteous flourish like a palm tree\nand grow tall like a cedar in Lebanon.|Keeps two durable trees contrasting with wicked grass.
92:13|Planted in the LORD's house,\nthey flourish in the courts of our God.|Preserves transplantation into sacred courts.

92:15|declaring, “The LORD is upright.\nHe is my rock; there is no injustice in him.”|Follows qere injustice and preserves the personal rock conclusion.

93:1|The LORD reigns, clothed in majesty;\nthe LORD is clothed in strength and has fastened it around himself.\nThe world stands firm; it cannot be shaken.|Keeps doubled clothing and the stabilized world.

94:5|They crush your people, LORD,\nand afflict your inheritance.|Retains crushing violence and people-as-inheritance.
94:6|They kill the widow and the resident foreigner;\nthey murder the fatherless.|Keeps specific vulnerable groups and actual killing.
94:7|They say, “YAH does not see;\nthe God of Jacob pays no attention.”|Retains the short divine name and quoted denial.
94:8|Understand, you senseless ones among the people!\nYou fools, when will you grow wise?|Keeps the challenge addressed within the people.
94:9|Does the one who planted the ear not hear?\nDoes the one who formed the eye not see?|Preserves planted ear and formed eye as creation arguments.
94:10|Does the one who disciplines nations not correct—\nthe one who teaches human beings knowledge?|Keeps the unfinished appositional structure without inventing a third question.
94:11|The LORD knows human thoughts:\nthey are only a breath.|Retains breath as the image of futility and transience.
94:12|How fortunate is the person you discipline, YAH,\nthe one you teach from your instruction,|Keeps YAH and the instructional purpose of discipline.
94:13|giving relief from days of trouble\nuntil a pit is dug for the wicked.|Preserves temporal until and the reversal awaiting the wicked.
94:14|For the LORD will not cast off his people\nor abandon his inheritance.|Retains paired nonabandonment promises.
94:15|Judgment will again accord with righteousness,\nand all the upright in heart will follow it.|Keeps restored justice and the responsive upright community.
94:16|Who will rise for me against evildoers?\nWho will take a stand for me against those who do wrong?|Preserves the personal plea and parallel rising/standing.
94:17|If the LORD had not helped me,\nI would soon have made my home in silence.|Retains death's silence image rather than a direct substitution.
94:18|When I said, “My foot is slipping,”\nyour faithful love, LORD, held me up.|Keeps the bodily stumble and sustaining love.
94:19|When anxious thoughts crowded within me,\nyour consolations brought me joy.|Retains inner multiplicity and consolation's enlivening effect.
94:20|Can a throne of destruction be allied with you,\none that uses law to fashion misery?|Preserves institutional wrongdoing through law without modern political insertion.
94:21|They band together against the life of the righteous\nand condemn innocent blood.|Keeps deadly conspiracy and judicial condemnation.
94:22|But the LORD has become my stronghold;\nmy God is the rock where I take refuge.|Retains both defensive images and personal assurance.
94:23|He will turn their wrongdoing back on them\nand destroy them through their own evil.\nThe LORD our God will destroy them.|Preserves the repeated severe ending and their evil's recoil.
95:1|Come, let us sing for joy to the LORD;\nlet us shout to the rock of our salvation.|Keeps communal invitation and the rock title.

95:6|Come, let us bow down in worship;\nlet us kneel before the LORD who made us.|Preserves embodied worship and human creation.

95:7|For he is our God,
and we are the people of his pasture,
the flock in his hand.
Today, if you hear his voice,|Keeps people/flock imagery and the transition into the warning.

and the peoples with his faithfulness.|Preserves doubled coming and distinct righteousness/faithfulness.
97:1|The LORD reigns! Let the earth rejoice;\nlet the many coastlands be glad.|Keeps worldwide shoreline/island scope.
